dedupe_keys.name: opengeosys ogs 6 open source finite element framework for coupled thermo hydro mechanical chemical processes in porous and fractured media

description: OpenGeoSys is an open-source finite-element framework for simulating coupled thermal, hydraulic, mechanical and chemical processes in porous and fractured rock and soil. The project site read on 2026-09-28 gives release 6.5.9, more than 990 benchmark tests and 69 interactive notebook tests, about 760 citing papers, and three main application areas: groundwater flow and contaminant and coastal transport, geothermal heat extraction and storage, and deep geological repositories for nuclear waste; a Zenodo archive of September 2026 carries a release whose notes cover two-phase thermo-hydro-mechanical processes and reactive transport coupled with PhreeqC in parallel. Coverage is generic, for any subsurface model the user builds. The code is free under the BSD-3-Clause licence, with documentation, a model hub and source code on the project's GitLab. Caveats: the programming language and build requirements were not read, and setting up coupled models needs specialist input data and expertise. It supports subsurface infrastructure studies, such as sizing borehole thermal energy storage for district heating, assessing groundwater drawdown around well fields, or evaluating the long-term safety of a nuclear waste repository. Related record: the AREHS OpenGeoSys workflow for a deep geological repository.
